NETLIFY IDENTITY SETUP

1. Deploy the extracted project through a connected Git repository or Netlify CLI. Do not use Netlify Drop because the live owner dashboard requires a server-side function.
2. In Netlify, open Project configuration > Identity and select Enable Identity.
3. Under Registration preferences, select Invite only.
4. Invite each authorised user from the Identity users page.
5. Assign one of these roles to each user:
   - framework: may open /portal/ and read the complete worked framework.
   - owner: may open /portal/ and /owner/, retrieve live Netlify Forms submissions, and calculate weights.
6. Ask the user to follow the invitation email, create a password, and sign in at /login.html.
7. If a role is changed, ask the user to sign out and sign in again so the refreshed token contains the new role.

IMPORTANT
- HTTPS is required. The normal *.netlify.app address already uses HTTPS.
- The public questionnaire remains at /index.html.
- The public site exposes only the questionnaire. The framework and analysis pages are not linked from any public page.
- Netlify's role-based redirect rules protect /portal/* and /owner/* at the CDN edge.
- The owner dashboard is stored only under /owner/; no root owner.html alias is included because Netlify Pretty URLs can otherwise resolve the alias before the protected directory.
- Invitation links that return to the questionnaire are forwarded automatically to the private account-activation page.
- Add NETLIFY_SITE_ID and secret NETLIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN environment variables before deployment. The access token stays in the server-side function and must never be added to public JavaScript or HTML.
- The dashboard retrieves new submissions every 15 seconds. CSV import remains available as a backup.
- The current weighted result is saved in the owner's browser local storage so the protected framework page can display it.
